← Back to Ultharness YOUR FIRST CLIENT PROJECT

A clear start.
A better finish.

Connect your tools once. Give each project a good brief. Keep the work, checks, and review in one place.

1. Make room for the work.

Download Ultharness 0.3.1 for an Apple silicon Mac running macOS 14 or later. Open the disk image, drag the app into Applications, and launch it.

This local build is ad-hoc signed and not Apple-notarized. The dashboard includes Node, npm, and npx. Your coding agents, provider accounts, model services, and client project dependencies remain separate.

Download the Mac app ↓

2. Connect a client folder.

Create a dedicated folder for the client’s website. In the Mac app, choose File → Connect Project Folder. In the dashboard, you can also add an existing folder under Projects.

The standalone app stores its workspace under ~/Library/Application Support/Ultharness/workspace. A compatible, already running browser server on port 4310 may be reused instead.

3. Bring your coding agents.

Install and sign in to Codex or Claude Code separately. Ultharness checks whether their executables are available. Your CLI account and provider configuration determine which models can run.

For model routing, start your installed OmniRoute service. In Model routing, save its gateway URL, test the catalog, and choose a model. A successful catalog test doesn’t verify upstream quota, authentication, or coding ability.

4. Connect the right context.

In Connections, add the project’s design link, repository, local brief, API docs, or other references. Select these when you create a client brief.

  • References: links and project-relative documents supply context. Saving a link doesn’t sign in to that service or automatically fetch its contents.
  • MCP: connect a separately configured local stdio or Streamable HTTP server, then list the exact read tool names you want the builder to use. Server behavior and credentials must be configured outside the brief.
  • Models: use your CLI defaults or the selected OmniRoute model. Ollama and its model weights are installed separately when you want local inference.

Keep credentials in local service or CLI configuration, never in the client brief, connection notes, URLs, or command arguments.

5. Define “done” before “go.”

Open Client deliveries → New client brief. Describe the audience, purpose, pages, user flows, content, visual direction, technology, responsive behavior, constraints, and expected handoff.

Add one measurable acceptance criterion per line. Choose a builder and reviewer. The reviewer uses a fresh session; you can use the same CLI or another one.

Add required files and/or finite npm verification scripts from the client project’s package.json, such as build, test, or test:e2e. A file assertion can use index.html :: Contact to require literal text. Use meaningful browser and accessibility tests for visual or interactive requirements.

Checks execute project code as your Mac user, with a two-minute limit per script. A passing build or an existing file alone doesn’t establish a working website.

6. Approve a bounded cycle.

Select a repair limit from 0–5, save the draft, and use Review & start to inspect the folder, agents, model route, checks, and selected connections.

Approve & build authorizes that cycle, including its bounded repairs. The maximum AI run count is 2 × (repair limit + 1). Model usage may be billed by your configured provider. The app doesn’t enforce a monetary budget.

Use Stop cycle to cancel the current step and hold later work. Missing tools, provider errors, malformed review verdicts, and an exhausted repair limit stop for attention.

7. Inspect. Accept. Then publish.

Recorded checks gate review. A reviewer assesses every acceptance criterion, and rejected work can go back for repair. Work that passes becomes Ready for your review.

Inspect the website and download its Evidence report. Choose Accept delivery or Request changes. Client feedback requires a new cycle approval. Publishing, messaging clients, and modifying production services remain separate actions.

AI review is an assessment, not a guarantee. Your chosen agent and provider may receive the instructions and project context they use, even though task records and reports are stored locally.

The small habits that help.

Use ⌘K / Ctrl+K to find pages, task numbers, and deliveries. Start with Inspect workspace to get a real local inventory. Use Routines for repeated checks while the server is on, and inspect the logs when a task needs attention.

The current release is for a single user on a trusted machine. Keep your local database private; logs and reports can contain project information.
